rationale: Independent reading: held EO 9593 (10 FR 9379, July 25, 1945) authorizes the Secretary of War to seize and operate the Springfield Plywood Corp. plants under the War Labor Disputes Act (paras. 1-5); para. 5 is a conditional own-end (possession to end within 60 days after productive efficiency is restored) with no held determination. Held EO 9603 (10 FR 10960, signed Aug. 25, 1945, 'Termination of Possession of Certain Property Taken by the Government') orders that all property seized under listed orders 'shall be returned to the owners thereof as soon as practicable' and lists 'No. 9593 of July 25, 1945'; listed orders in conflict are amended. Every operative paragraph of 9593 is ancillary to the seizure, so a direction to return all property taken under it exhausts the order. My status: NO (functional end; first-end date depends on the unheld actual return, correctly left unadjudicated). D6: the only history lead is OFR 'See: EO 9603'; a search of held texts for 'No. 9593'/'9593 of' finds only EO 9603 (and same-page neighbours 9602/9604); no re-seizure, extension or amendment. Accept, non-fatal note: 'as soon as practicable' fixes no date.
